gap: No result ChatGPT got states the break-even months between the three pricing models: Spytec Pulse OBD month-to-month ($0 hardware, $14.95/mo) is the cheapest way to track a car for up to 7 months, Bouncie only undercuts it from month 17, and on Spytec's annual plan ($107.40/yr) Vyncs Basic does not become cheaper until year 7.
standout_why: Compared against cited rottenwifi.com, vyncs.com/pricing.aspx and bouncie.com/pricing, plus uncited hotairtag.com (subscription costs and Bouncie vs Vyncs), allinsider.net, tagandtether.com and Vyncs's own comparison page. Rottenwifi lists the input prices but no totals. Hotairtag already prints 1-year and 3-year totals (Bouncie $206/$437, Spytec $107/$322), so the totals themselves are not new; it uses a stale $39.99 Vyncs activation fee and leaves the Vyncs 3-year total blank. Tag & Tether says only that a subscription device is 'cheaper in year one and more expensive in year four', with no month. None states a break-even month, the one-month trial outlay, or the distance a car covers between updates.
decides: It makes the pick depend on how long the shopper needs tracking. For a short need (a teen's first months, a loaned or stored car, a trial) Spytec Pulse OBD month-to-month wins: $14.95 to start, against $99.64 for Bouncie and $145.98 for Vyncs, and it stays cheapest through month 7. For a year or more, Spytec's annual plan at $107.40/yr beats Bouncie at every horizon ($98.39 less in year 1, $115.19 less over 3 years) and beats Vyncs Basic through year 6. Bouncie is the cheaper choice only against Spytec's month-to-month rate, and only from month 17. On update rate, Vyncs Basic's 3-minute transmit means about 3.25 miles between map points at 65 mph against 0.27 miles for Bouncie; Spytec's interval could not be sourced, so the page should not claim a speed advantage for it.

findings.value: Month-to-month is cheaper for needs of 7 months or less

findings.note: Year 1: $205.79 − $107.40. Three years: ($89.99 + 36 × $9.65 = $437.39) − (3 × $107.40 = $322.20). Spytec's $8.95/mo is below Bouncie's $9.65/mo and has no hardware charge, so the gap widens by $8.40 a year.

findings.label: Break-even: Vyncs Basic 4G+ vs Spytec annual plan
findings.note: $45.99 ÷ ($107.40 − $99.99) = 6.2 years. After 6 years Vyncs is $645.93 against Spytec $644.40; after 7 years Vyncs is $745.92 against Spytec $751.80. Three-year totals: Vyncs $345.96, Spytec $322.20. Assumes both renew at today's prices.

findings.label: Distance between map points at 65 mph
findings.value: About 3.25 miles (points sent every 3 minutes); 1.08 miles between 60 s samples
findings.note: 65 mph × 3/60 h = 3.25 mi; 65 × 1/60 = 1.08 mi. The pricing page lists Basic at 60 s GPS sampling with points sent every 3 minutes, and Pro at 20 s with points sent every minute.

findings.label: Distance between map points at 65 mph
